meta.name: Images of the World and the Inscription of War
meta.description:
Captures the gap between what an image records and what anyone sees in it. Allied reconnaissance planes photographed Auschwitz in 1944 while aiming at a factory next door; the camps sat in the archive, fully observed and entirely unseen, for three decades. Farocki builds the whole film from that one distinction — this might be the closest any film gets to your projection framework, stated in evidence.

Farocki’s intriguing and troubling film explores the processes of visual perception and how they affect our understanding of history and society. In a work reminiscent of the writings of Paul Virilio and Michel Foucault, Farocki examines a range of phenomena including aerial reconnaissance photos of the Auschwitz concentration camp.
